To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mast cells are involved in tumor progression, that they are recruited by tumor cells, that their products (histamine, heparin and proteases) promote tumor progression and that tumor cells are able to induce the production of these products by mast cells.
mast cells are involved in tumoural growth, and that this involvement is due to the secretion of mast cell-derived mediators such as proteases, heparin and histamine.
mast cells are not only involved in allergic reactions but also in tumour progression and metastasis, by promoting tumour angiogenesis and cell invasion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of mast cells on tumour progression.
the possible association of mast cells with the progression of tumoural lesions.
the study of the interactions between mast cells and tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mast cell accumulation around tumors may be the result of both, an immune response against tumours and a pro-tumoral activity.

, mast cells are not a tumor-promoting factor, but that the accumulation of these cells in the vicinity of tumours may be a result of the tumoural process and that mast cells products may contribute to tumor growth and metastasis.
mast cells could be both for or against tumours, depending on the type of tumours and the experimental conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, mast cells are not always a tumour's ally but that their role is not always to fight against tumour growth.
the accumulation of the mast cells around the tumour areas is the result of an immune response against tumour.

mast cells are not tumour promoting cells per se, but that the accumulation of these cells is a consequence of tumour progression, and that the mast cell's products may contribute to tumour expansion and metastasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of mast cell in tumour growth and development remains unclear.
mast cells are not simply bystanders of tumour progression but rather active players of the process.
mast cells are not only involved in tumour progression but also, that mast cell-tumor cell cross talk is essential for mast cell accumulation.
